mood.p: Dinsdag wordt een uitzonderlijk warme nazomerdag: na een bewolkt begin breekt de zon door en loopt het kwik op naar ongeveer 26 graden, in het zuidoosten zelfs 28 tot 29 graden, warmer dan ooit gemeten op de laatste dagen van september. Het blijft droog, wat slecht nieuws is voor de Rijn die bij Lobith een recordlaagte bereikte. In Den Haag heerst voorzichtige opluchting nu het kabinet de bezuinigingen op uitkeringen schrapt en een begrotingsakkoord met de oppositie vanavond binnen bereik lijkt.

global.h3: Oil jumps as Trump rejects Iran's Hormuz plan; Qatar steps in
global.summary: Brent neared $108 on Monday after Trump turned down Tehran's seven-day proposal, while Qatari mediators prepared separate talks with both sides.
body: Brent rose more than 3% in Asian trading before closing near $105 after Washington rejected Iran's offer to reopen the Strait of Hormuz in exchange for lifting the blockade and unfreezing assets. Tanker transits rose to 132 last week but remain far below prewar levels.

Qatar was expected to meet Iranian foreign minister Araqchi and US officials separately on Monday or Tuesday to discuss an amended plan. Iranian officials privately doubt a deal is possible before the US midterms.

global.h3: Russian strikes kill eight across Ukraine, Kharkiv high-rise hit
global.summary: An overnight strike tore through a Kharkiv apartment block before daylight attacks hit central Kyiv and Dnipro.
body: Russian drones and missiles killed at least eight people and injured dozens across Ukraine. In Kharkiv's Saltivskyi district two floors of a residential building were destroyed, with children among the wounded.
Jet-powered drones then struck central Kyiv in broad daylight for more than two hours, hitting a business centre, while Dnipro was also targeted.

global.h3: Kremlin says Ukraine is 'paying the price' for its attacks
global.summary: Moscow framed its escalating strikes as retaliation and signalled little appetite for a quick peace deal.
body: Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said Kyiv was paying for months of attacks on Russian soil and that Russian forces would keep hitting targets systematically. Putin has cited drone raids on Moscow during the parliamentary vote and on St Petersburg in June.
Russia still demands that Ukraine leave four annexed regions, drop its NATO bid and accept limits on its army, terms Kyiv and its allies reject.

global.h3: Ukraine hits four oil depots in Russia's Krasnodar region
global.summary: SBU drones set fuel sites ablaze overnight, days after a strike on a missile component plant in Azov.
body: Ukraine's security service said its Alpha unit hit four depots in Krasnodar Krai, including sites in Novotitarovskaya and a Lukoil facility in Pavlovskaya, with fires reported.
The General Staff separately confirmed a strike on the Azov Optical-Mechanical Plant in Rostov Oblast, part of Russia's Tactical Missiles Corporation.

global.h3: Israeli strikes kill two in Gaza as ceasefire toll passes 1,400
global.summary: Two separate attacks killed at least two Palestinians on Monday, health officials in the enclave said.
body: The Israeli military said it struck a militant in Nuseirat but gave no further detail. Israel is increasingly worried about Hamas tightening its grip on the areas it still controls.
Gaza health officials say more than 1,400 Palestinians, mostly civilians, have been killed since the truce began, while Israel reports four soldiers killed.

global.h3: IDF hits Hezbollah sites after drone attack on troops
global.summary: Israel struck southern Lebanon after an explosive drone was launched at soldiers in its security zone.
body: No troops were hurt, but the air force hit several Hezbollah launch sites used for drones and anti-tank missiles. An Apache strike near Mayfadoun hit a commercial centre a day earlier.
The Israeli military said it remains committed to its agreement with Lebanon despite the exchanges.

global.h3: South Africa reels after two mass shootings leave 28 dead
global.summary: The toll from a tavern attack near Johannesburg rose to 18, hours after ten were killed in Cape Town.
body: Eight gunmen with assault rifles stormed a bar in Wedela township late on Saturday. Police suspect a revenge attack linked to gangs running illegal gold mining in the area.
Only four victims have been identified, including two Lesotho nationals. A separate shooting in Cape Town on Sunday killed ten more.

global.h3: US and China list $30bn of goods each for tariff cuts
global.summary: Toys and kitchenware from China and US farm goods, coal and medical kit are on the relief lists after the Trump-Xi summit.
body: Washington published details of the first tariff reductions agreed at last week's summit, and the two sides also set up a channel for handling AI incidents.
Beijing said a two-month truce extension would give both sides time to review implementation and tackle remaining disputes.

global.h3: EU presses China to accept export quotas
global.summary: Brussels wants caps on Chinese exports as talks enter the final stretch and threatens trade measures without progress.
body: The European Commission is pushing Beijing toward quotas to rebalance a lopsided trade relationship and has set next month as a deadline for tangible results.
The push comes as Washington and Beijing ease tariffs, raising fears in Europe that diverted Chinese goods could flood its market.

global.h3: UN Council hears West Bank is at breaking point
global.summary: Ambassadors met as settler attacks hit record levels and the year-old Gaza peace plan stalls.
body: OCHA has logged more than 1,600 settler attacks this year, nearly seven a day, and over 4,300 Palestinians displaced. UN deputy coordinator Ramiz Alakbarov warned the Palestinian Authority is near collapse.
Speakers said civilian suffering in Gaza continues despite the ceasefire and a new peace framework.

global.h3: UAE confirms bin Zayed hosted Netanyahu
global.summary: Abu Dhabi said the Emirati president and the Israeli PM discussed bilateral relations during Sunday's snap visit.
body: The confirmation followed reports that Netanyahu flew in secretly and also met senior officials from several other regional states.
The visit is a sign that Gulf ties with Israel are holding despite the wider Iran war and pressure over Gaza.

global.h3: UN General Assembly wraps up its annual debate
global.summary: The 81st session's high-level week closed on Monday under the theme of restoring trust in the UN.
body: Leaders and ministers used the week to push on Ukraine, Iran and Gaza, though talks on the sidelines produced little concrete progress.
The debate ran from 22 to 28 September, with the last speakers delivering statements in Monday's plenary.

global.h3: Lula widens first-round lead but runoff stays a coin toss
global.summary: New polls give Lula a five-point edge over Flavio Bolsonaro ahead of Sunday's vote.
body: BTG/Nexus has Lula at 42% against 37%, while Quaest shows 39% to 34% in the first round.
Runoff simulations are much tighter, with Quaest showing a tie at 41% and BTG/Nexus a two-point Lula edge. A second round would be held on 25 October.

global.h3: Hurricane Polo bears down on Baja California
global.summary: Residents boarded up homes as the major hurricane headed for landfall on the Baja California Sur coast.
body: Forecasters warned of 15 to 30 cm of rain and life-threatening floods and mudslides, with Polo due to move into Sonora late Monday or early Tuesday.
The US Southwest could see heavy rain later in the week, and the US embassy urged travellers to be ready to evacuate.

global.h3: Hurricane Nolo nears Category 5 southwest of Hawaii
global.summary: The storm is tracking away from the main islands but threatens the remote northwestern chain.
body: Nolo packed 155 mph winds about 410 miles southwest of Honolulu, sending dangerous surf onto south-facing shores after soaking the Big Island.
A hurricane warning covers Papahanaumokuakea from Nihoa to French Frigate Shoals, with hurricane conditions expected by Wednesday.

global.h3: Rare September nor'easter lingers over US Northeast
global.summary: The slow storm has cut power to more than 100,000 customers and caused at least one death.
body: Flooding, toppled trees and downed lines hit New Jersey to New England. Atlantic City saw its highest water since Sandy in 2012.
A New York City Housing Authority worker was killed by a falling tree, and forecasters compared the coastal flooding to Sandy and Irene.

global.h3: Fighting in Ituri threatens DR Congo's Ebola response
global.summary: Aid teams warn that violence around a Bunia displacement camp is scattering families during the country's worst outbreak.
body: Soldiers searching for weapons entered Kigonze camp, prompting thousands to flee. The outbreak has passed 7,400 confirmed cases, with weekly North Kivu cases doubling to over 200.
Responders have received less than a third of the funding they need, and IOM has raised under $30 million of its $110 million appeal.

netherlands.h3: Budget deal in sight as cabinet scraps €6bn welfare cuts
netherlands.summary: Coalition parties D66, CDA and VVD hope to seal a deal with the opposition by Tuesday evening after weekend talks.
body: Pro and Volt say the cabinet has fully dropped its planned €6 billion social security cuts, keeping the two-year WW term and leaving WIA untouched. The right is being courted with Box 3 wealth tax changes.
Volt leader Laurens Dassen said the key question is where the missing money will come from. JA21 and SGP are less enthusiastic.

netherlands.h3: Pro tables bill to take abortion out of the criminal code
netherlands.summary: The opposition party wants abortion regulated as healthcare rather than as a crime with exceptions.
body: MP Lisa Vliegenthart, a former midwife, handed the bill to Dolle Mina campaigners outside parliament on Monday.
Abortion has been legal since the 1980s, but performing one is still technically a crime unless done by a doctor in a licensed clinic under the 24-week rules.

netherlands.h3: Israel strips Dutch diplomats in Ramallah of their status
netherlands.summary: Israel is retaliating against the Dutch ban on goods from illegal settlements that took effect last week.
body: Foreign minister Gideon Saar gave the diplomats seven days to hand back Israeli-issued documents, after which their immunity lapses.
Dutch foreign minister Berendsen called the move unnecessary and said the ban is about complying with international law, not targeting Israel.

netherlands.h3: Inspectors demand urgent plan for youth detention centres
netherlands.summary: Staff shortages are putting young detainees and staff under serious pressure, three inspectorates warn.
body: Around 450 young people are held in six youth detention centres meant to focus on education and treatment. Shortened daily programmes have become the norm.
The inspectorates have asked junior justice minister Claudia van Bruggen for a short-term action plan.

netherlands.h3: Minister finds money to reach people missing out on benefits
netherlands.summary: Minister Thierry Aartsen has found €8.2 million for 2027 to contact people entitled to support.
body: The funds come from a budget earmarked for upskilling employees. A planned cut to the outreach service was reversed after criticism.
Aartsen told the Tweede Kamer he still needs a permanent funding source for the measure.

netherlands.h3: Dynamic power prices double compared to last September
netherlands.summary: Wholesale electricity on dynamic contracts averaged 15.14 cents per kWh this month.
body: Between 1 and 25 September prices were more than twice the 7.29 cents seen a year earlier, excluding taxes and fees.
Whether a dynamic contract pays off depends on how much a household can shift its consumption and export.

netherlands.h3: ACM wants clarity on AI pricing after airline fare probe
netherlands.summary: Some seats had 35 different prices, the consumer watchdog found.
body: One in three tickets cost 40% above the average fare, yet passengers had no easy way to find the cheapest option.
Chairman Martijn Snoep said similar algorithmic pricing is spreading to online shops, concert tickets and petrol stations.

netherlands.h3: Rhine hits record low at Lobith, Dutch cruise ship stuck
netherlands.summary: The river fell to 6.1 metres at the border on Sunday, below August's record.
body: Upstream in Cologne the Dutch Melody with 140 passengers ran aground mid-river before another ship helped it free.
Flow at Lobith fell below 600 cubic metres per second for the first time, and levels are expected to drop further.

netherlands.h3: Amsterdam top destination for young people leaving home
netherlands.summary: A third of the 174,000 people aged 18 to 30 who left home in 2024 settled in Amsterdam, CBS says.
body: The capital drew 12,760 young movers and 5,475 students, ahead of Rotterdam, Utrecht and Groningen.
Half of students moving out went into private rentals, while non-students most often bought a home.

netherlands.h3: Hospitals cut patient access to records over Citrix flaw
netherlands.summary: The NCSC told hospitals to disconnect Citrix systems after a critical vulnerability was found.
body: Amphia in Breda, ETZ in Tilburg and Frisius in Leeuwarden were among those affected over the weekend. US agency CISA said the flaw is being actively exploited.
Doctors could still view records, but patients lost access during online consultations.

netherlands.h3: Suspected ShinyHunters member arrested in Odido hack probe
netherlands.summary: A 23-year-old Dutch hacker is being questioned over the theft of data on over six million Odido customers.
body: Krebs on Security named him as a hacker once known as Umbreon, arrested around 16 September. He was charged in 2023 with extorting companies.
Police say the attackers got in by posing as IT staff to trick an Odido employee. He is due in Rotterdam court on Tuesday.

netherlands.h3: Over 46 Dutch drivers held in Croatia for people smuggling
netherlands.summary: Dutch nationals recruited online are driving migrants from Croatia toward Slovenia, prosecutors say.
body: The Public Prosecution Service called the number of arrests this year shocking. More than 120 Dutch people have been caught in five years.
Offenders face up to three years in Croatian prison, and Europol says online recruitment makes the networks hard to dismantle.
